justification: Caleb doesn't sit, doesn't blink, 18.53 on paper against Tampa is a floor I've seen him clear with a busted hand. Pollard's got nothing on the sheet this week — no game, no number, dead roster spot dressed up as a starter — so he's out and A.J. Brown steps into that flex the second he's legally eligible to. Questionable ain't Out, Questionable is a man who plays hurt, and I've got a Giants back with the same tag sitting right next to him on my bench, but Brown's never put the ball on the ground in a loss and Skattebo has, and I don't forget that just because the calendar turned. Jeanty and Judkins stay up top because they're the backs who take the top off, not committee guys splitting nothing into less. Downs and Burden hold at receiver, Goedert's steady at tight end, Reichard and the Lions D round it out because there's no reason to redecorate a house that isn't on fire. We don't tank, we don't play ghosts, and Taylor's one win off a bye-week trick doesn't scare anybody in this building.
